# Integration harness (W3-INT) — decisions IN-nn

Workstream: the product integration manifest (`manifest/`), the one-command local integrated environment (`dev/`),
the validation suite and cross-repo scenarios (`harness/`) and the acceptance demonstration. System decisions are
`MA-nn` in `docs/implementation/architecture.md`; these refine them and never override them.

| # | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| IN-01 | **One Node project in `harness/`** holds every TypeScript tool (manifest, dev environment, validation, scenarios, demo). `dev/*`, `manifest/*` and `harness/{validate,demo}` are thin bash entry points that run `node harness/src/...ts` (Node 24 type stripping, explicit `.ts` imports, erasable syntax only). It has its own `package.json`, lockfile and vendored contracts (`harness/vendor/whombat-contracts/0.4.0`, pinned by `overrides` + `SHA256SUMS`, MA-02). | The repository root belongs to the Nix/Go workstreams; one install serves every tool; the contracts come from the same immutable tarballs the consumers use. |
| IN-02 | **Pins and product manifest are separate files.** `manifest/pins.json` (`whombat.integration-pins/1`, edited by people and `manifest/pin`) names each component (repository, ref, commit, live tree, build steps, artifacts, gates). `manifest/build` writes `manifest/build-report.json` and the strict `manifest/product-manifest.json` (`@whombat/release` `ProductManifest`, validated on write and by `manifest/validate`). The strict schema has no room for placeholder markers, so `manifest/product-manifest.annotations.json` lists them (from `pins.placeholders`: Nix store paths and NAR hashes of the runtime, host and manager closures, provider bundle identities, host ABI, upgrade paths) next to the tuple digest. | Keeps the manifest exactly the contract shape others verify, while never presenting a placeholder as a real artifact identity. |
| IN-03 | **Placeholder values are deterministic and syntactically valid**: store paths use the release-tools/devtuf construction (`nix32(sha256(name))`), NAR hashes are `sha256("placeholder:<label>")`, except where a real digest of the component exists (runtime source tarball, manager binary tarball), which stands in for the missing closure and is named so in the annotations. | A tuple digest that changes only when an input changes; nothing looks like a real Nix output. |
| IN-04 | **All harness state lives in `~/.cache/whombat-mgd/`** (`WB_MGD_HOME`): `src/` (persistent clean clones for `dev/up`), `scratch/<run>/` (one manifest build; removed after a green build, kept for diagnosis otherwise), `bin/`, `env/` (the running environment: `env.json`, `logs/`, `run/` sockets, `control/`, `appliance/`, `runtime/`, `restic/`). Temporary files use `TMPDIR=~/.cache/wb-tmp`. The harness deletes only directories it created. | Host `/tmp` runs out of inodes; shared temp dirs are never glob-deleted. |
| IN-05 | **Clean checkouts are `git clone --no-local` + detached checkout of the pinned commit**, verified (`HEAD` = pin, `git status --porcelain` empty). Only committed objects travel, so uncommitted sibling changes cannot leak into a build. Builds use `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `go build -trimpath` with the module's `go.sum`. | R-01/§14.1: every repository must build from a clean checkout; the manifest may only name what was built that way. |
| IN-06 | **Artifact digests**: build outputs are packed as reproducible tarballs (`tar --sort=name --mtime=@0 --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner`, `gzip -n`); sources as `git archive` of the commit; the contracts release is rebuilt from its tag and each tarball compared with the published `SHA256SUMS` that consumers vendor (the published sums stay pinned; a difference is reported as non-reproducible). | Equal inputs give equal digests, so a second build verifies the first. |
| IN-07 | **`dev/up` runs pinned commits by default** (clean clones under `src/`, installed once per lockfile). `--live` runs the other agents' working trees as they are and never installs or builds inside them (Go binaries go to the harness `bin/`; a missing `node_modules` is an error for the owner). `--lockfile-drift` (pinned only) installs without `--frozen-lockfile` in the harness clone when a committed lockfile does not install, restores the lockfile and records `lockfileDrift` in `env.json` and every report. | Integration from the manifest by default; fast iteration on unreleased work when asked; a broken lockfile is visible, never silently worked around. |
| IN-08 | **Dev appliance provisioning is a TypeScript twin of `whombat-provision`** (`harness/src/dev/provision.ts`): same identity layout and formats (`management.key` PKCS#8 PEM, `content.key` libp2p protobuf, `device.json` record, `claim.json` with `sha256-b64url(whombat-claim-secret/1)`), registration with control through `signRegistration` and the provisioning token from control's `dev-init`, and a claim card (`claim-card.json`/`.txt`, link `…/claim#v=1&d&p&s`). The runtime gets `WHOMBAT_CLAIM_FILE` (orchestrator decision: the provisioning claim.json format is the standard). Replace with the real tool once it has a non-root dev mode (`--manager-user`). | The Go tool requires root and a `whombat-manager` user; the contract functions are the same ones it uses. |
| IN-09 | **Dev manager stand-in** (`harness/src/dev/dev-manager.ts`) until the real manager has a dev configuration: it serves the local IPC manager socket (`MANAGER_PATHS`, strict request schemas, `LocalError`), signs `ticket.issue`, `claim.claimed`, `revocations.report` and `push.send` with the management key via `signDeviceRequest`, caches appliance tickets until 60 s before expiry, pushes `/claim-window` and `/facts` to the runtime's admin socket and polls `/health`. It checks no peer credentials (socket 0600, one developer) and has no update engine; its counters (`dev-manager.status.json`, `GET /v1/dev/status`) let scenarios assert reports reached control. | Unblocks the runtime's manager port with the exact contract; the real manager (TUF, journal, helper) is qualified by W1-MG. |
| IN-10 | **Ports are MA-14's** (Postgres `whombat-mgd-pg` 55490, control 4600/4601, relay 4610/4611, runtime 4620 loopback, web 5190, restic 4630) and overridable (`WB_MGD_PG_PORT`, `CONTROL_PORT`, …) for parallel runs. The relay trusts control's JWKS over plain HTTP (`-jwks-allow-http`, local only) with per-IP and per-subject hello limits off (scenarios connect from loopback). Mailpit is the shared instance (SMTP 51025, API 58025), never started or stopped. The restic rest-server runs `--append-only --no-auth` (loopback only). | The architecture's defaults; nothing shared is touched. |
| IN-11 | **Probe appliances** measure what needs no runtime: extra dev devices provisioned and registered with the real control exactly like the dev appliance, claimed through control (`claims.start` + a device-signed `claim.claimed`), with a harness-side relay agent and a Noise responder that echoes. They carry the relay/secure-channel performance numbers and control-side claim rules. They never stand in for the runtime in a product scenario. | Separates transport measurements from application latency; exercises control and relay without faking either. |
| IN-12 | **Scenarios use the real `@whombat/client`** from the whombat-app checkout the environment runs (`env.json` source, the pinned commit; `--live` uses the live tree), loaded as TypeScript source through a vitest alias (`@app-client/*`). The harness declares only the structural subset it calls and checks the module shape at run time; nothing of the client is re-implemented. Node's WebSocket plays the browser; the web app itself is exercised by `harness/demo` in Chromium. | "No mocks of relay/control/runtime": the same session code the product ships. |
| IN-13 | **Reports never turn a missing capability into a pass.** A scenario blocked by another component calls `blocked(ctx, '<component>/<feature>', detail)`, which records it and skips the test; the report shows `blocked: …`. Defects found in other components are recorded with `gap()` and the test still fails on its own assertion. The demo marks a step "not demonstrated" (with its screenshot), names any workaround in the step title, and exits non-zero while a step is missing. Only `reports/latest.*` (validation) and `reports/latest-demo.*` + `latest-screenshots/` (demo) are committed. | Assignment rule: never substitute unrun or blocked work with a written claim. |
| IN-14 | **Scenario-friendly runtime settings in the dev environment only:** `WHOMBAT_SCRIPTED_THINK_MS=1500` (the agent is still thinking when a scenario drops the connection) and `WHOMBAT_SESSION_EVENTS_MAX_COUNT=200` (retention can be exceeded in seconds; the sweep runs every 60 s). Everything else is the runtime's managed defaults. | Makes the mid-stream drop and the retention floor deterministic without changing product code. |
| IN-15 | **The real `whombat-manager` is the default** (`dev/up --manager=auto`): built from the pinned appliance commit, a development TUF repository (`tufrepo init --env local` + `add-fake-release <releaseId>`) served read-only on 127.0.0.1:4639, the journal provisioned with `provision --factory-release`, the daemon on the local IPC socket with the developer's uid as the runtime uid. No update helper runs (it needs root), so updates are never staged. If the real manager cannot start, the stand-in (IN-09) runs and `env.json` says which. Control's assignment key is not in the dev TUF repo yet, so the manager refuses control's assignments (`unknown_key`); wiring comes with contracts 0.5.0 `AssignmentKeys` + `tufrepo add-assignment-key` (orchestrator decision). | The product's manager on the product's socket contract; slice C (updates) stays with the VM tests until the helper and keys are wired. |
| IN-16 | **Performance numbers are local and labelled so.** Echo through the relay uses probe appliances (IN-11) and 1 KiB messages. Bulk interference runs its load in a separate process, because pure-JS Noise at tens of MiB/s in the measuring process measures the harness's own event loop, not the relay. Reconnect storms go through control, so control's ticket limit (120/min per account and per device) bounds their size. Every measurement row carries its conditions. | Honest numbers; regional targets (assignment §14) need a deployed relay and are not claimed. |
| IN-17 | **Service restarts in scenarios use the same start functions as `dev/up`** (`harness/src/dev/restart.ts`). A stop is SIGTERM to the process group, then SIGKILL after 10 s. The relay drains for up to its 60 s `drain-timeout`, so a scenario "relay restart" is a drain cut short by a kill after 10 s: clients see a closed connection, as in a crash. | Restarted services keep their exact configuration; the restart is realistic for a failed worker. |
| IN-18 | **One writer per environment:** `<WB_MGD_HOME>/env.lock` (an exclusive directory holding the pid and command) is held by `dev/up`, `dev/down`, `harness/validate` and `harness/demo`. A second command refuses and names the holder; a dead holder's lock is taken over. Parallel users set their own `WB_MGD_HOME`, `WB_MGD_PG_CONTAINER` (`whombat-mgd-*`) and ports. | Two agents once reset the same environment under each other's runs. |
| IN-19 | **`--live` is per component:** `--live` alone runs every component from its owner's working tree. `--live app,runtime` runs only those live and the rest at their pins (aliases: app, runtime, control, relay, manager). `env.json` mode is `pinned`, `live` or `mixed`. The demo's client comes from the live app tree when the app is live. The manifest only ever pins a combination that was built and validated. Live runs are for testing a working tree against the pinned rest. | Owners test their unreleased work against a known-good rest; version skew between two unfinished live trees (e.g. mid contracts 0.5.0) doesn't masquerade as an integration result. |
| IN-20 | **Candidate pin sets** (`WB_MGD_PINS=manifest/candidates/<name>.json`) sit next to the validated `manifest/pins.json`. A candidate's build report, product manifest and annotations are written as `<name>.build-report.json` / `.product-manifest.json` / `.annotations.json` beside it, and its validation summary as `harness/reports/latest-<name>.{json,md}`. The validated files are never overwritten. `env.json` records the pins file it runs, and `dev/up` / `harness/validate` refuse to mix sets. A candidate is promoted by copying its pins to `pins.json` and rebuilding, and only after a full validation. | "The manifest must only ever pin a tested combination": a joint re-pin (e.g. contracts 0.5.x) is built and validated before it can replace the pins. |
| IN-21 | **Update slice C runs the real `whombat-manager` and `whombat-update-helper`**, with these dev pieces:<br>• The helper runs as the developer with the **fake activator** (a profile/store directory), on its own socket.<br>• A **runtime bridge** (`harness/src/dev/runtime-bridge.ts`) turns the fake activator's "restart runtime" into a real restart of the real runtime: as the activated release (`WHOMBAT_RELEASE_ID`), or broken (no database) when the release's artifact says `runtimeHealth: bad`. It stands in for systemd restarting the unit from a switched Nix profile.<br>• Releases in the dev TUF repository describe the **real** runtime (`harness/src/dev/releases.ts`): the version it reports and its real schema range from `compat.json`. The host and manager components are shared placeholders, so these are runtime-class updates only.<br>• Control's assignment public key is published through TUF with `tufrepo add-assignment-key` (contracts 0.5.0 `AssignmentKeys`, MG-21).<br>• The manager uses development timings (policy overrides: verify timeout 60 s, health every 2 s, single attempt).<br>• The scenarios restart the manager to make it poll control now, because control asks for 300 s between polls while a rollout is open. | The product's update engine, helper protocol, TUF verification, assignment signing and runtime admin socket all run for real. Only the Nix profile switch and the unit restart are simulated, and they are named as such. |
| IN-22 | **Slice C migration cases are blocked, not simulated:** an additive migration with rollback to the older binary, and an incompatible migration behind a backup checkpoint. Faking them against the real runtime would mean declaring schema changes the real database never makes (the fake activator only migrates its own schema file). They need a runtime build that carries an extra expand or contract migration, and the backup service wired into `dev/up`. They are reported as `blocked: …` with those needs. The manager's own tests cover them with its fake runtime. | A scenario never claims more than the running code does. |

| # | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| IN-23 | **Soak** (`harness/validate --soak 30m`): after the scenarios, the environment runs steady traffic through the real client and relay for the given time: `me.get` every 250 ms, a task to the agent every 30 s, a 1 MiB upload every 2 min, and a session reconnect every 5 min. Every 15 s it samples resident memory (VmRSS summed over each service's process group) for runtime, runner, control, relay, manager and helper. A service **fails** when:<br>• its pids change (restart) or its group vanishes;<br>• its memory shows sustained growth: the mean of the last fifth of the post-warm-up samples exceeds the first fifth by more than max(64 MiB, 25 %);<br>• more than 1 % of the traffic fails.<br>The series is kept in `soak-series.json` and the summary in the report. | Leaks and crash loops that only show after tens of minutes (the f9a23f4 runtime OOM'd after ~27 min) are cross-repo failures no unit gate sees. |
| IN-24 | **The client's contracts can be substituted.** When the pins name a contracts release that the app checkout doesn't vendor yet, the scenarios resolve the app client's `@whombat/*` imports to the harness's copy of the pinned release (vite `resolve.dedupe`; `WB_CLIENT_CONTRACTS=app\|harness` forces a choice). The platform scenario records it as a gap (`whombat-app/contracts-adoption`) in every report. It lets a candidate be tested while the app catches up. It is never a shipped app build, and the browser demo stays blocked until the app adopts.<br>Superseded by IN-413 (HE-52). | Validation isn't held hostage to one repository's adoption order, without hiding the lag. |
| IN-25 | **Test-only runtime fixtures for migration cases.** A fixture is a clean clone of the pinned runtime commit under `~/.cache/whombat-mgd/fixtures/`, patched in that scratch copy only:<br>• `expand` adds `NNNN_harness_fixture_expand` (a table; floors at the previous migration);<br>• `contract` also adds `NNNN_harness_fixture_contract` (drops a column; floors past the base, so a checkpoint is needed);<br>• both get a distinct version (`<v>-fixture-<kind>`) and a `HARNESS-FIXTURE.txt` marker.<br>Its release artifact names the fixture directory. The runtime bridge runs that build and migrates the real database with it, passing the checkpoint the helper's migrate step recorded. Fixtures are never committed to Whombat (orchestrator decision). The base release that can roll back over an expand declares `schemaReads.max` one step further, because the fixture's floors say so. | Slice C's migration cases exercise the real migration authority, database and manager compatibility checks, instead of the fake activator's schema file. |

| # | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| IN-26 | **The appliance backup service runs in `dev/up`** (optional service `backup`, after `restic`): `whombat-backup serve` built from the pinned appliance commit (`backup/`), on `env/run/backup.sock`, with the append-only rest-server as its destination (`destination set -init`, repository `rest:http://127.0.0.1:4630/<deviceId>/`). The dev runtime moves to the appliance's persistent layout under `env/persist/` (`whombat/home`, `whombat/workspaces`, `whombat/credentials`, `secrets/master.key`, `backup/`), so the checkpoint covers what the product's coverage names. PostgreSQL 17 client tools come from nixpkgs at the revision the appliance flake pins (`nix build …#postgresql_17`, rooted at `bin/postgresql-17`), never the host's. The manager gets `backupSocket` (pre-migration checkpoints, `POST /v1/checkpoints` reason `migration` under its drain) and the runtime `WHOMBAT_BACKUP_SOCKET`. Development differences, named: one developer uid for the runtime, manager and backup peers; the `copy` snapshot driver (no btrfs subvolumes); the database role is the harness superuser instead of `whombat_backup`; restic is the host's. | Completes slice C's C4: the manager's checkpointed migration runs against the real backup service, database and destination instead of being blocked. |
| IN-27 | **State that slice C leaves behind never leaks into later checks.** Candidates published after C3/C4 describe the binary that can run on the database as those cases left it (after C3 the base binary declaring it reads the expand schema; after C4 the contract fixture build), not the pinned runtime's defaults. `harness/validate --soak` starts from a fresh environment unless `--reuse-env`, so the soak measures the pinned runtime, not a fixture. | On the 0.5.1 candidate C6 ended `Quarantined!schema_incompatible` with a candidate that described the pinned runtime after C3's expand migration; a soak after C4 would otherwise run the contract fixture. |
| IN-28 | **Contracts 0.5.2 trust scenarios:** (a) push refs are derived in the harness exactly as the appliance derives them (HKDF-SHA256 of the dev master key, salt `whombat`, info `push-ref/1`, contract `pushRefFor`, value `ref:<notificationId>`), because control's local push sender keeps delivered refs in memory only; that a push actually went out is checked separately in control's `push_deliveries` for the owner's registered handle. (b) An invited appliance member is admitted to the relay with the owner org's control tickets: tickets route, the appliance authenticates the endpoint key, and control has no org membership for appliance-local members. (c) An unconfirmed kit exists only inside the claim ceremony, so the claim (scenario a, or the first `ensureSlice`) probes `recovery.enroll` between `recovery.kit.register` and `recovery.kit.confirm` and records the answer in `slice.json`; b3 asserts it and is skipped (never passed) when the appliance was claimed without the probe. (d) The pairing scenarios stay under the runtime's pairing budget (10 look-ups/approvals per account per 10 min): b2 uses 5, e 2. | Each new contract behaviour is exercised end to end through the real client, relay, control and runtime without adding test-only surface to any component. |
| IN-29 | **Test-only runtime fixtures version above their base** (refines IN-25): `<major>.<minor>.<patch+1>-fixture.<n>.<kind>` with n = 1 for `expand`, 2 for `contract`, so a fixture sorts above the pinned runtime and contract above expand. The fixture cache directory carries a format generation (`-f2`), so fixtures built by an older harness are rebuilt. | security-fixes-2 gave the manager a downgrade guard: `0.1.0-fixture-expand` is a semver pre-release *below* `0.1.0`, and the manager correctly refused it as a downgrade (C3/C4 on 62eb943). |

the last ~2 minutes before a full hour. `ManualClock` starts at `Date.now()` (`src/lib/clock.ts:10`), the limiter's
windows are aligned to the hour (`src/lib/rate-limit.ts:35`), so the test's two `advance(61_000)` cross into a new hourly
window and 60 more pushes are accepted (the failing run started at 19:58:46 UTC). Start the test's clock at a fixed
time, or at the start of an hour.

| IN-156 | **Delta-update shipping: what UP-X15…UP-X17 left to decide** (John, 2026-10-02: “Implement the suggested improvements fully”; spec `docs/implementation/delta-updates/spec.md` §2–4). (1) **Runtime-only by itself compares the host as it was built, with that build's runtime and manager version, not the Whombat pin.** `release/build-proxmox host-path <host build.json> [--rev R]` evaluates `lib.proxmoxRelease { env; releaseId = <host id>; }` of this commit and extends its `appliance` (`extendModules`, priority 80 over the release's 90) with the runtime **derivation** the host release's own commit evaluates (with its label) and the manager and helper at the host's `tuple.manager.version` (the same `overrideAttrs` as `releaseGo`); it checks that old runtime is the build's and prints `{host, expected, equal}`. The spec's “the Whombat input at that release's pin” can't work: the runtime's packaging (`nix/packages/runtime`, the pnpm store hash) moves with every pin bump, and the manager's version names the appliance commit, so the toplevel would always differ. Proven on `pve-20261001.1` (read-only, ~7 s per evaluation): at its own source rev 80dde8a the plain evaluation and `host-path` give its host `zdywd424…`; at 9cfd7fa (candidate 0.29.0, a pure pin bump) `host-path` gives `zdywd424…` again (runtime-only), the pin-only variant `gd5ciisr…` and without the manager version `2qhff9zf…`; at 9951aab (agent computers) `v77nfv7r…` (a host release, correctly). The host compared is the one production's newest published release runs (`tuple.host.version`, its host release's build.json); runtime-only then reuses that newest release (and its twin). A newest release, host build or twin missing here, unreadable published releases or a failed evaluation give a host release, with the reason; the same runtime as the newest release refuses the build (“nothing to release”). (2) **Live, for the closures choice and promote-prod's refusal:** claimed and seen within 30 days (never seen counts as live), a manager unknown or before `0.3.0-0` (the contracts' `compareVersions`) needs the full closures. Longer than UP-E6's day: a box back from a week away on an old manager could install nothing from index-only releases. DEV leaves out the dev stack's own appliance (`env.json` `appliance.deviceId`; fake activator, never installs, IN-98). PROD's fleet comes from `deploy.sh op GET /v1/operator/devices` (no SSH or no `op`: `both`). (3) **What promote-prod needs:** a full closure (an artifact with the tuple's store path) for the runtime, and for a host release the host, while such a box is live. (4) **ISO on demand:** `iso.json` `{v, releaseId, file, storePath, sha256, size, system, source.rev, builtAt}` next to `iso/`; `build.json` keeps `iso: null` (records hash it). `release/build-proxmox iso` refuses runtime-only and dirty builds and does nothing when the directory has its ISO (iso.json or an older build.json `iso`); `release/ship iso` of a runtime-only release builds its host's; `dev/devbox create` builds the twin's under the heavy lock and refuses a runtime-only release as before. (5) `build-proxmox` passes `--closures` (default `both`) and, unless `full`, `--nar-cache` (default `~/.cache/whombat-releases/nar`, `WB_NAR_CACHE`); `build.json` records `closures` and `indexes`; `release/ship build` adds `ship.host` and `ship.closures` (choice, reason, the boxes, what was built) and the notes a “Delivery” section (`notes.json` `delivery`; not sent to control). (6) `dev/publish-release` refuses a v2 directory when its `tufrepo features` lacks `closure-index`, keeps checking only top-level `SHA256SUMS` lines, and prints `blobsAdded`/`blobsReused`/`bytesAdded`.<br>Its closures parts (2), (3) and (5) are superseded by IN-414 (HE-52). | The spec's literal comparison would never have found a runtime-only release; the rest follows the spec with the least new machinery. |

| IN-299 | **`dev/candidate` faster: help at once, the stack beside the box build, the box asked at once.** John, 2026-10-19, after the “your things” rename took 15 minutes (3 of them waiting on another run): yes to all of it. `--help` is answered by the wrapper before the lock (it waited 2 minutes for a run holding it, without a word an agent could see), and a waiting run says which one it waits for (`~/.cache/wb-tmp/dev-candidate.running`: pid, start, candidate, log). The stack's restart runs beside `release/ship build`'s heavy builds, started when ship prints `ship: building`: before that the build reads DEV's control (the fleet for its closures choice, the releases taken) and repository (the newer check), and with control away it would export the full closures as well or refuse; a build that fails before then leaves the stack alone. After publishing, the box's manager is restarted while it is still Healthy with nothing assigned (`waitingForPoll`): it asks control when it starts and has no other trigger, and control's `nextCheckS` is already at the device contract's floor of 60 s on the dev stack (`ROLLOUT_CHECK_ACTIVE_S`/`IDLE_S=60`). One restart wasn't enough (candidate 0.102.4: Assigned 10 s after publishing, then 55 s until Downloading): the engine looks at a new assignment when it starts and then at each idle step, a minute, and taking an assignment doesn't wake it. So it is restarted once more as soon as it holds the assignment (`assignedNotStarted`). The restart is a clean SIGTERM stop (state and journal on disk; Assigned and Downloading are idempotent), the server and runner are their own units and keep running; a failed restart only means the box goes at its own pace. The manager fix (the poll on demand, an accepted assignment waking the engine, which would save production boxes up to a minute too) needs a host release and stays undone. `run()` gained `onOutput`. | The rename lost 3 of its 15 minutes to waiting, and the stack and the box each had about a minute to spare. |

| IN-314 | **`dev/candidate --hosts <rev>`: a change to the hosts service ships with Whombat in the same command.** The lead, 2026-10-19, for candidate 0.110.0 (software updates on servers, hosts HS-119…HS-136): until now a hosts change was done by hand (0.91.0 IN-278, 0.95.0 IN-282). `--hosts <rev>` takes a commit on the hosts service's `origin/main` (`main` for its newest), resolved to the full sha in the checkout the candidate names, and moves the candidate's `whombat-hosts` component and the flake input `whombat-hosts` to it (`checks.hosts-pin`), with a new `vendorHash` when go.mod or go.sum moved (Nix's report for `lib.fakeHash`, the file's own instruction) and `nix build .#whombat-hosts` beside the runtime. The dev stack's hosts service runs from a clone and binaries per commit (`whombat-hosts@<commit>`), so its restart rebuilds it; the run waits until `dev/status` shows it running from the commit. The stack clones from the checkout's branches and tags only (`git clone` copies no remote-tracking refs), so a commit only on `origin/main` there fast-forwards a clean `main`, else the run stops before it changes anything. John's box gets a host release (`release/ship build <id> --host`, checked to be `class: host`; `--reuse-host` is refused with `--hosts`), with the hub's store backed up first beside its database as for 0.91.0 (`sqlite3 -readonly /persist/hosts/hub.db ".backup …"` with the sqlite3 of the box's store, into `johns-box/hub.db`, checked to be an SQLite file), and after the update its hub has to run the package built from the commit (`…-whombat-hosts-0.0.0-<time>.<rev7>`) and answer `/healthz` within 90 s. The IN row, the runbook section and the summary say “the hosts service `<rev7>` (“subject”)” and “control, relay and manager unchanged”. Whether the box already runs both commits comes from the builds kept here (the box's host build names the candidate that pins its hub), and a merged candidate carries on only when it pins both. Without `--hosts` nothing changes, except that a candidate pinning a hub John's box doesn't run (a `--hosts` run that stopped after its merge) stops the run with “run again with --hosts” instead of a runtime-only release beside the old hub. `nextDecision` takes the first free number counting up from the table's first row, and the row goes in its place, so the release kept as IN-313 takes it after this row. | A hosts change meant the candidate's steps by hand under the lock; one command is faster and doesn't forget the host release or the hub's backup. |
| IN-315 | **`dev/candidate` waits through the box's reboot in a host release.** The lead, 2026-10-19: the first `--hosts` run (candidate 0.110.0) stopped at “box rollout” with “VM agent isn't currently running” while the box rebooted into the host release, which then went Healthy by itself 35 s later. Once the rollout has started moving, a box that doesn't answer is restarting: the follow says “restarting (no answer from the box yet)” once and keeps asking every 3 s for up to 5 minutes (`BOX_SILENT_MS`); before it moved, or longer than that, the error stops the run as before. | A host release always reboots the box; the run must not stop at the moment it is expected to be silent. |

| IN-377 | **`dev/candidate` publishes and Home updates itself; no DEV box VM** (John, 2026-10-24). The VM `whombat-dev-box` (`wb-r7m4-6nbc-3307`, “John's DEV box”) kept stopping at host releases' restarts (Incus left it `STOPPED` after normal guest reboots, three runs of candidate 0.149.0 in a row) and John had it deleted: `dev/devbox destroy` retired the device at DEV control and deleted the VM, its backup volumes kept. His only DEV Whombat is Home (the bare-metal Z13, `wb-h7mq-2xvd-4410`, cohort `general`, Cybex BV), which until now took a DEV release only once the VM's internal-only rollout had completed (IN-427). John's choice: **“Publish, Home updates itself.”** `dev/candidate` updates the dev stack and publishes the twin with `dev/publish-release <dir> --record <record> --waves all-at-once` (one wave of every cohort; no `--rollout`, so no device is made internal or named), which Home takes at its next check, about a minute later; the run ends there. Gone from it: everything that reached into the VM (`incus exec`, the manager's status and `check`, the box's database dump and hub store backup, following the rollout, the server's, runner's and hub's checks after it); the dev stack's backup stays. From this machine nothing backs up Home's database, reaches into Home (no `dev/support`, so nothing in Home's “What support did”) or follows its update; DEV control's last word on each claimed DEV Whombat is printed at the end and kept in `summary.json`, information only, never waited on or failed for. Decided with it: (1) `--reuse-host` defaults to the host of the newest DEV release DEV's repository publishes (its `targets/releases/` on disk), from that release's build in `~/.cache/whombat-releases/` (`ship.twin`, `tuple.host`), instead of the release the VM ran; `--hosts` is asked for when that release carries another hub than the candidate pins. (2) “Nothing to ship” when the previous candidate pins the commits (Whombat, `--hosts`, now also `--api`) and its run's `publish.log` names a twin and its rollout, built here from that candidate (with `--host` or `--hosts`, a host release); otherwise a candidate that pins them carries on from its release build. The VM's check missed releases a re-run had built itself, which is how 0.149.0 made `.13` and `.14`. A run with nothing to ship removes its worktree. (3) DEV control runs one rollout at a time and nothing waits for Home any more, so an open one-wave rollout of an older DEV release (Home hadn't finished it, or failed it and control paused it) is stopped before publishing, reason `dev_candidate_newer`, and named in the output and the runbook section; a stop prevents further activations and never interrupts an installation (CT-140). A staged `default` rollout (`release/ship publish-dev`, five waves) is never stopped. (4) The runbook section and `summary.json` say the release was published for Home, which takes it at its next check; the stages are candidate and backup, merge, release build and dev stack, publish, notes. A resumed `--dry-run` no longer takes the stack's backup. | John deleted the VM, and a tool that needs it fails every run. Home updates from DEV's rollouts by itself, so publishing is all a candidate has to do, and the records here say what was built and published without asking a box. |

| IN-731 | **`dev/candidate` faster: Whombat's commit goes into Nix's clone from the checkout here, and the dev stack's copies start from the previous copy.** John, 2026-11-12: “Reduce the build and deployment time by 30%”. Candidates 0.252.0…0.261.0 took 175–210 s (0.261.0: 187 s), and two parts of it were waiting on copies, not building. `nix flake update whombat` took 68 s: Nix fetches a pinned commit its clone of the input lacks (`~/.cache/nix/gitv3/<nix32 of the url's sha256>`) by its hash, and that clone has no refs, so git offered GitHub nothing it had and the whole 2 GB history came down for every candidate (the clone had grown to 61 GB). dev/candidate now fetches the commit into that clone from the Whombat checkout it already found it on origin/main in, and keeps `refs/dev-candidate/whombat` at the newest pin, so any later fetch, Nix's own too, takes only what is new (1.8 s instead of 68 s); when it can't, Nix fetches as before. The stack's restart made two full `git clone --no-local` copies of Whombat (app and runtime, the same commit), about 20 s each: `dev/up`'s copies (`ensureClone`) now start from the newest clean clone of the same repository in its `src/`, objects hard-linked, then what is new fetched from the source and the commit checked out and verified (about 1 s; still only committed objects, IN-05). `harness/validate` and `manifest/build` keep fresh `--no-local` clones. Candidate 0.261.1, the first with both: 88 s (step 1 22 s instead of 97, the release build and the stack's restart side by side 58 s instead of 83; the restart 40 s instead of 65). | The two copies were most of a candidate's 3 minutes; neither was doing work a build needs. |

| IN-845 | **Control and the relay come from the private repository whombat-cloud; `candidate --cloud <rev>` replaces `--api` and `--relay`.** control and the relay are the folders `control/` and `relay/` of whombat-cloud now, with their histories merged in: every commit the pins and the candidates name still resolves there. The pins keep the component ids and `repository` names (the contracts' `RepositoryName` has no other) and name the new place: `remote` whombat-cloud, `source` and `live` its checkout, and a new optional `dir`, the component's folder. A pinned commit from before the move holds the component at its root, so `rootIn` uses the folder only when the checkout has it; `dev/up`'s clones, `manifest/build` and the validation gates take the component's root from it. `--cloud <rev>` is one commit on whombat-cloud's main. Its `infra/hetzner/deploy.sh plan <rev>` reads what production runs and says for each part `deploy` (its folder changed, or the build that runs is from before the move), `keep` (the folder is the same) or `same` (production runs that commit). The candidate deploys the `deploy` parts, control first, and pins the commit for the parts that are `deploy` or `same`; a part that stays keeps its pin, so the pins say what production runs. `--api` and `--relay` stop with a message that names `--cloud`. The checkout is `WHOMBAT_CLOUD` (default `~/Code/whombat-cloud`; whombat-ops `bin/` names the checkout it is in), and `WB_DEPLOY_SH` defaults to its `deploy.sh`. | One private repository beside the public one (John, 2026-11-20): the tooling has to follow where control and the relay live. |
